default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-908.title: VWAP sigma-band fade
E-908.hypothesis: Price far below/above VWAP in units of its own recent deviation is stretched; liquidity providers anchored to VWAP lean against it and price snaps back.

E-909.title: EMA stretch in ATR units fade
E-909.hypothesis: A close several average bar-ranges away from a short EMA is an overextension from forced liquidation or chasing; fade the first bar that gets there.

E-910.title: Bollinger band re-entry
E-910.hypothesis: A close outside the band followed by a close back inside shows the push was absorbed; trade back toward the mean.

E-911.title: Volatility squeeze release
E-911.hypothesis: When recent dispersion is far below its typical level for this time of day, resting orders pile up on both sides; the first range break releases stops and continues.

E-912.title: Staircase of higher lows
E-912.hypothesis: Consecutive bars each with higher low and higher close show persistent absorption of sellers; participants chasing keep it going.

E-913.title: Dollar lead, index lag
E-913.hypothesis: WIN and WDO are negatively linked through foreign flow; after a large WDO move that WIN has not yet mirrored, the index catches up in the opposite direction.

E-914.title: Minute-of-day seasonality
E-914.hypothesis: Scheduled flows (opening auctions, fixings, hedging) repeat at the same clock minute; follow the sign of the average next-bar return at this minute over the last 20 sessions when it is consistent.

E-915.title: New-extreme clustering
E-915.hypothesis: Several fresh session highs (lows) inside a short window mean one side is repeatedly lifting the offer; stop-driven flow persists.

E-916.title: Day-open stretch fade with reversal bar
E-916.hypothesis: When the price is far from the session open relative to the typical distance at this time, and a bar turns against it, late chasers are trapped; fade back toward the open.

E-917.title: Wide reversal bar through prior body
E-917.hypothesis: A bar much wider than recent ones that closes near its extreme and through the previous opposite bar's open shows aggressive new flow overpowering the last move; follow it.
